args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and check why it was promoted even though it failed in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It didn't need change-manager approval because it has been healthy in production before.
- **After the rollback:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks are passing, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure and the rollback. It asks for a root-cause check on v2.3.1 before it's redeployed.

One thing to look into: v2.3.1 was already failing in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) before it was promoted to production. I noted this in the incident.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
